Ever since about 200lbs I've been having trouble with my breathing, but also, the blood-rush from clenching all those big muscles is starting to get very bothersome. But, that's turned out to be the cause of several minor form problems because it prevented me from keeping my core properly tensed. How long between squat reps is acceptable?

Not sure if that answered what you were asking.

Wow, I don't think about it nearly that much. I take a breath at the top, hold my breath on the way down, and exhale on the way up. But I never had to think about my breathing, it was just natural. Maybe on the last couple reps on the last set I'll take an extra breath at the top.

I inhale as I drop and naturally exhale coming up. Especially after two plates if I'm struggling. Between sets, well I train with an HR monitor because I'm into that. So I usually wait until my heart rate comes down to about 100bpm. About a minute or so.
I keep a timer/stopwatch on hand and tend to limit my breaks between repetitions to 90 seconds.
That's crazy! You're standing under a loaded squat bar for over a minute between reps?

My level is more the result of a need to survive and a lifetime of training than a desire to be a bodybuilder. By the time I was your age, I'd been doing weighted squats of just over three times the weight you're doing reps at for well over a decade. I didn't do it every day, nor did I reach this point overnight, but I did do it consistently and cautiously progressed. I've been lifting since before I was out of elementary school. I had to get strong, because guys who were naturally taller and stronger than me took me as an easy target and acts of violence tends to escalate as a child grows older if left undefended.

You have two issues here.

  1. Don't worry about catching your breath between reps. When you are trying to hit a 5x5 PR damn right you won't be able to crack out 5 reps in 5 breaths. Take a breathe, hold it, squat down and up, then release your breath. Take a few breaths so you don't pass out then squat again.

  2. If you are "plateauing" (can't beat your PR) you may need to switch up your program. Stronglifts is a beginner program. After ten months of linear progress it is understandable if you can't keep up that pace. Check out the "texas method"as an example intermediate program. It's similar to stronglifts, but you only go heavy once a week which lets you recover

My beginner program was starting strength a 3x5 thing and it took me way too long to realize it was time to switch up my program. It's impossible to squat 3x per week with a 5lb increase each workout for 11 months. I blamed my diet, my protein intake, lack of sleep, skipping days here and there. Switched up my program and now I'm setting squat PRs again! Good luck :)
